items.en: Does Quintus want Syra to go away?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; answer Nōn or Minimē, or say what he does want (accusative + infinitive after volō)

items.q: Quid Quīntus Syram sibi nārrāre iubet?
items.en: What does Quintus order Syra to tell him?
items.hint: the accusative object of nārrā

items.q: Quāle mōnstrum Quīntus in fābulā audīre cupit?
items.en: What kind of monster does Quintus want to hear about in the story?
items.hint: an adjective agreeing with mōnstrum (the sentence has it in the ablative after dē)

items.q: Cui mōnstrō corpus hominis, caput bēstiae est?
items.en: Which monster has a man's body but a beast's head?
items.hint: the dative of possession ('to whom there is…')

items.en: Quintus isn't a timid boy, is he?
answers: Minimē, Quīntus nōn est puer timidus
items.hint: num expects the answer 'no'; the sentence is an indirect statement after nōlī putāre

items.en: Where did the Minotaur live?
items.hint: the ablative after in (place where)

items.en: By whom had the labyrinth been built?
items.hint: the agent of a passive verb: ā/ab + ablative

items.en: From where did Daedalus come to Crete?
items.hint: place from which: ex + ablative, with the city name in the ablative

items.en: What did the Minotaur eat?
items.hint: the accusative object after praeter ('nothing except…')

items.q: Quandō adulēscentēs virginēsque Athēnīs in Crētam mittēbantur?
items.en: When were young men and maidens sent from Athens to Crete?
items.hint: an adverb of time

items.q: Cūr nāvis Athēniēnsium vēla ātra gerēbat?
items.en: Why did the Athenians' ship carry black sails?
items.hint: a reason clause with nam/quia; the colour is an ablative of means

items.en: Who was ruling Crete then?
items.hint: the subject of regēbat, in the nominative

items.q: Cūr rēx Mīnōs Athēniēnsibus male volēbat?
items.en: Why did King Minos wish the Athenians ill?
items.hint: a quod clause giving the reason; its verb is pluperfect passive (necātus erat)

items.en: What kind of man was Theseus?
items.hint: an adjective describing him that takes a genitive (patriae amāns, glōriae cupidus)

items.en: What did Theseus decide to do?
items.hint: the infinitive that completes cōnstituit

items.en: How was Theseus' ship fitted out?
items.hint: an ablative of means (with what)

items.en: Who had the name Ariadne?
items.hint: dative of possession with nōmen est

items.en: When did Ariadne begin to love Theseus?
items.hint: a cum prīmum clause ('as soon as') with the perfect indicative

items.en: How will Theseus come back to Ariadne?
items.hint: an ablative of means (auxiliō + genitive)

items.en: What did Ariadne give to Theseus?
items.hint: the accusative object of dedit (Thēseō is the dative receiver)

items.q: Quō Thēseus fīlum post sē trahēns intrāvit?
items.en: Where did Theseus go in, dragging the thread behind him?
items.hint: the accusative object of intrāvit (the place he went into)

items.en: How did Theseus get out of the labyrinth?
items.hint: a perfect participle of a deponent verb (secūtus = having followed), active in meaning

items.q: Cūr Thēseus cīvēs suōs ā mōnstrō servāvit?
items.en: Why did Theseus save his fellow citizens from the monster?
items.hint: ob + accusative ('on account of')

items.en: Didn't Ariadne board Theseus' ship?
items.hint: nōnne expects the answer 'yes' (Ita / Ita est); the sentence also has ad + gerund (ad fugiendum)

items.q: Quō Thēseus cum fīliā rēgis nāvigāvit?
items.en: Where did Theseus sail with the king's daughter?
items.hint: the name of an island in the accusative, with no preposition, for place to which

items.q: Quis Ariadnam dormientem in īnsulā relīquit?
items.en: Who left Ariadne sleeping on the island?
items.hint: the subject in the nominative

items.en: From where did Ariadne look out at Theseus' ship?
items.hint: place from which: ex/ab + ablative (she climbed onto the rock, unde = from where she looked out)

items.q: Cūr Aegeus sē dē saxō in mare iēcit?
items.en: Why did Aegeus throw himself from the rock into the sea?
answers: quod arbitrātus est fīlium mortuum esse
choices: quod vēla alba in nāve vīdit
items.hint: the deponent participle arbitrātus ('having judged') introduces an indirect statement (accusative + infinitive)

items.q: Quis dē saxō sē in mare iēcit?
items.en: Who leapt off the rock into the sea?
items.hint: the subject in the nominative (sē refers back to him)

items.en: For how many years did Theseus rule Athens?
items.hint: accusative of duration of time (for how long)
